turns.user: Our ERP sales report shows duplicate invoice rows after joining invoices to invoice_lines and customer_tags. A quick fix would be SELECT DISTINCT to hide the duplicates. Diagnose the likely cause and recommend the safest next step.
turns.assistant:
The likely cause is row multiplication: each invoice joins to multiple `invoice_lines` and multiple `customer_tags`, producing a many-to-many combination. For example, 3 lines × 2 tags can yield 6 rows for one invoice.

`SELECT DISTINCT` may hide identical projected values, but it does not reliably restore one row per invoice and can mask incorrect totals or differing line/tag data.

Safest next step: define the intended invoice-level output, then aggregate or pre-aggregate each one-to-many relationship separately before joining—for example, summarize invoice lines by invoice and aggregate tags by invoice. Validate the result against known invoice counts and totals before changing the report query.
